text:
incident-bot: Paging on-call for P1: Amaranth (enterprise) degraded traffic in us-east-1 affecting dedicated pool amaranth-pool-east1. Impact: increased 5xxs and ~20% request drop. Runbook: regional failover recommended if warm capacity available. @alice_oncall, please ack and assess.

alice_oncall: ack. I’m on it. seeing elevated 503/504 from the edge -> origin path, started tailing logs.

marco_sre: looking at the pool metrics now. CPU is fine but we have persistent connection errors to tenant VPC peering in us-east-1. Peering route flap maybe.

shivam_eng: confirm: this is the dedicated pool for Amaranth with direct VPC peer + private LB, right? Not the hosted API customers?

alice_oncall: correct — amaranth-pool-east1. their control plane is healthy, just data path to the tenant VPC experiencing intermittent drops.

katie_support: customer reported API errors at 09:12 their time. They’re seeing request timeouts and partial responses. They asked for ETA.

leah_account: I’m on the bridge with the Amaranth ops lead. We should give them a mitigation plan asap. Can we prepare an interim routing change?

marco_sre: two options: 1) shift tenant traffic to their warm standby pool in eu-west-1 (already provisioned) OR 2) try a DNS-level cutover to a regional alias to force routing via their VPC cross-region peering. Given the peering instability, option 1 (traffic shift to eu-west warm pool) is safest.

alice_oncall: I’ll kick the traffic shift. Steps: spin up warm nodes in eu-west (if not warm), update route policy to prefer eu-west for Amaranth tenant id, signal the LB to drain us-east. Also set DNS TTL to 60 to shorten switchover.

shivam_eng: commands I’ll run now:
```
# scale the dedicated pool (if not already warm)
redwoodctl pools scale amaranth-pool-eu-west --replicas 6 --min-ready 3
# update routing policy to route tenant by tag
redwoodctl routing set-policy --tenant amaranth --preferred-region eu-west-1 --reason "emergency failover"
```

dns_ops_bot: Note: changing DNS TTL for amaranth.example.enterprise from 300 -> 60 will take ~10s to apply in control plane. External caches may take longer.

marco_sre: I see the eu-west pool health checks passing for warm nodes. Initiating routing policy now. Expect gradual shift within ~30s of policy commit.

alice_oncall: switched routing policy to prefer eu-west-1. Starting drain of active connections on us-east pool.

ops_handoff: handoff note: I’m taking the active mitigation. I’ll watch for error rate changes and customer telemetry. If errors persist >5m after shift, we’ll perform a DNS CNAME cutover to the eu-west VIP (manual step, needs DNS approval).

katie_support: telling customer: "We detected a regional network instability impacting your dedicated pool in us-east-1. We are actively shifting traffic to your warm standby in eu-west-1 to restore service. Expect progressive recovery in the next few minutes. We'll confirm once stable."

leah_account: customer acknowledged and appreciates the transparency. They asked to keep the old pool warm so we can fail back once peering is healthy.

marco_sre: metrics update: 5xx rate on amaranth is down from 18% -> 4% within 90s of policy change. Latency increased ~60ms for a subset due to cross-region hop but successful responses returned.

alice_oncall: rolling monitoring: set alert threshold lowered to catch regressions. Also logging a short-lived config to keep TTL at 60 for 30m to ensure rollback window is small.

dns_ops_bot: DNS TTL changed -> 60. External propagation in flight.

ops_handoff: continuing to observe. Will not perform DNS CNAME cutover unless customer agrees or errors climb. Preparing post-incident notes for root cause: likely peering BGP flap between our us-east fabric and customer VPC.

katie_support: customer wants a quick RCA and plan for remediation. Leah, can you coordinate SLA credits conversation once RCAs are out?

leah_account: yes, I’ll coordinate. For now they just want a full timeline and confirmation of warm pool strategy.

marco_sre: creating incident tracker ticket and linking packet captures + BGP logs.

alice_oncall: last update before handing off: traffic shifted, errors back to baseline, customer informed, warm pools left active, will continue watch. Handoff to ops_handoff for the 1hr stabilization watch.

ops_handoff: ack. I have the bridge and will escalate to network team if any peering flaps recur.

incident-bot: Incident P1 (Amaranth regional): status RESOLVED->DEGRADED->MITIGATED. Timeline and actions added to ticket. Please attach any follow-up tasks.

ops_handoff: closing slacker notes here, moving to postmortem draft.

katie_support: thanks team — will send final customer update in 10m. :thumbsup:
